questions.prompt: Read this line from the notice board of a youth centre in Tozeur: "Every July, the rules of the centre are read aloud by its founder to the volunteers who have just joined." Which words are the subject of the sentence, that is, what the sentence tells you something is done to?

options.text: the volunteers who have just joined

questions.explanation: "the rules of the centre" is the subject: the verb are read agrees with it, and the rules are what the reading is done to. "its founder" is the agent, the person who does the reading; an agent stands after by, and it is never the subject of the sentence it appears in. "the volunteers who have just joined" are the people the rules are read to, which the word to announces; they listen to the rules, but the rules, and not the volunteers, are what is read. And "Every July" answers when: a time phrase may stand in front of the verb, as this one does, and it is still never the subject.

questions.prompt: Emna is writing a poster for her school's human rights club. Complete it: "The campaign is almost ready. We only need ___ from each of you, and it will be finished by Friday."
questions.explanation: "a little help" is right: help cannot be counted, so it takes a little, and a little means exactly what the poster means, a small amount that is nevertheless enough. "a few help" puts in front of an uncountable noun the quantifier reserved for things you can count one by one, as in a few posters or a few members. "a lot of help" is correctly built, but it means more than enough, and the poster says only need and almost ready, so the quantity announced is small. And "a lot help" loses the word of, which belongs to the expression and never disappears from it: you write a lot of help, a lot of time, a lot of members, always with of.

questions.prompt: A notice on the wall of a workshop in Bizerte reads: "Every ___ in this workshop is paid at the end of the month." Which word fills the gap?
questions.explanation: "employee" is the word: the ending -ee names the person on the receiving end of the action, here the person who is given work and who is therefore paid. "employer" carries the opposite ending: -er names the one who does the action, the person who gives the work and pays for it, so the notice would be saying that the owner pays himself. "employment" is not a person at all but an abstract noun, the fact of having work, and a fact cannot be paid. And "employ" is the verb; after every the sentence needs a noun, not a verb.

questions.prompt: In a report about a village school, you read: "The classrooms were repainted last August by the pupils themselves." Who did the painting?
questions.explanation: "The pupils." is right: in a passive sentence the doer, when it appears at all, comes after by, and here the sentence ends with by the pupils themselves. "The classrooms." is the subject, and the subject of a passive sentence is what receives the action; classrooms are painted, they paint nothing. "The village school." is taken from the sentence that introduces the quotation, not from the quotation itself, which never presents the school as a doer. And "The sentence does not say." would be the honest answer for a passive sentence with no by phrase, but this one has a by phrase and it names the painters.

questions.prompt: Lesson fifteen gives one meaning to each of its new words. Which of these four words names the difficulty of living without enough money or enough food?
questions.explanation: "hardship" is the word: it names conditions of life that are hard to bear, and the lesson uses it for a family that lacks money, food or shelter. "evidence" names something else entirely, the facts that prove that a thing is true, which has nothing to do with being poor. "burial" is the ceremony of putting a dead person in the ground, an event and not a way of living. And "a penalty" is the punishment fixed for breaking a rule, so it is something a person is given, not something a family simply lives through.
